value: What anatomical features of the inferior colliculus of genetically epilepsy-prone rats account for the initiation and propagation of audiogenic seizures?

Assembles the authors' anatomical work into a circuit account of audiogenic seizures in genetically epilepsy-prone rats: the central nucleus of the inferior colliculus contains excess GABAergic and total neurons whose number tracks seizure severity, and it initiates seizures that propagate via its projection to the external nucleus and on to the superior colliculus.

quote: This review provides a summary of the data that show a role for the IC in audiogenic seizures.

Finally, the use of knife cuts through the midbrain indicated that the ICCN sends an important projection to the external nucleus and that this projection plays a vital role in the propagation of seizure activity from the site of seizure initiation in the ICCN.
Previous studies have shown the functional importance of the inferior colliculus (IC) for the propagation and initiation of audiogenic seizures in several models of epilepsy in rats.

value: Seizure activity initiated in the ICCN is carried out of the colliculus along the bilateral ICCN-to-external-nucleus projection and onward to the superior colliculus and pontine reticular formation.
quote: Both results from our study of lesions in the coronal plane (Ribak et al. 1994) and anatomical studies that show the ICCN projects bilaterally to the EN (Coleman and Clerici 1987; Saldafia and Merchfin 1992) support the hypothesis that this pathway conveys seizure activity.

The inferior colliculus (IC), so named for its position relative to the superior colliculus (SC), is a major relay nucleus in the midbrain for ascending auditory information en route to the ipsilateral medial geniculate body of the thalamus.
It is generally agreed that three subdivisions exist in the IC of mammals (Fig. 1): the central nucleus (ICCN), external nucleus (EN), and the dorsal cortex (DC)

quote: Genetically epilepsy-prone rats (GEPRs) exhibit convulsions when exposed to sound stimulus, and the seizures are scored on a 0-9 scale (0 being no seizure, and 9 being one fit of wild running and an accompanying tonic seizure, culminating in tonic hind limb extension).
